messages:
alex: quick q — during Dedicated -> Hosted fallback, whose responsibility is eviction priority and operator metadata propagation? we're losing operator tags and the SLO attribution/telemetry is noisy.
mira: hmm, are we talking about the lease-level eviction (affinity) or the replica eviction on the dedicated pool? :thinking:
alex: lease-level. tenant gets routed to hosted when dedicated capacity is exhausted. Dedicated had metadata like `operator=tenant-pool-a` and `eviction-priority=low` that disappears on fallback.
tj: we saw this in the 04/03 incident — hosted treats fallbacks as new tenancy and defaults priority=normal. that bumps requests into different QoS buckets.
sophie: can we surface operator tags in the handshake so hosted can inherit them? maybe a short-lived token with metadata that hosted can trust for attribution.
devon: that implies the control plane must vouch for the token. risks: spoofing if token is leaked, and complexity if private deployments don't want external tokens.
alex: agree. idea: add a minimal handshake extension on the routing side: `X-Redwood-Lease-Meta: base64(operator=...,eviction=...)` signed by controlplane key. hosted validates signature.
mira: simpler: let routing proxy attach the raw metadata to the request as internal-only headers (strip on ingress) and add an audit log entry for the attach. avoids new token plumbing but relies on trusted edge.
tj: downside — when cross-cloud routing happens, those headers might be dropped. signed token is portable.
sophie: we should also think about telemetry correlation. If operator tag is stripped, attribution in tracing/metrics breaks. we need consistent `trace.parent` + `redwood.operator` propagation.
ops-bot: Incident 2024-04-03: fallback-attribution-gap recorded. Suggested fix: include `operator` claim in lease token. See RFC-215 for token format.
devon: regarding private deployments: some customers run their own controlplane; signed tokens still work if they share certs or we require customer-managed KMS to sign. opt-in flag `propagate-operator` in manifest.
alex: proposal: two-part compatibility path:
1) short-term: routing attaches internal-only headers and controlplane emits audit event. low-effort but non-portable.
2) long-term: lease-token v2 (signed claims: operator, eviction_priority, manifest_version). hosted validates signatures from controlplane CA or customer CA for private mode.
mira: +1. also add a fallback policy in hosted: if eviction_priority missing, consult `legacy-priority-mapper` which uses tenant history to avoid SLO jumps.	
sophie: and add a small test harness in repo infra/handshake-tests that simulates Dedicated->Hosted fallback and asserts operator preserved.
tj: quick nit: we need TTL on the token and rotation semantics. tokens should be single-use or short-lived (<= 60s) to reduce replay risk.
devon: logging: include `fallback.original_pool` and `operator` in the audit logs for postmortem and billing reconciliation.
alex: actionable checklist:
- design token v2 claim set and signing model (who signs in hosted vs private)
- implement routing header attacher quick patch (internal-only)
- add hosted validation + legacy mapper fallback
- add handshake e2e test and update playbooks
- ops-runbook: how to revoke/rotate controlplane signing certs
sophie: i'll take the test harness + runbook. devon can own the audit/log schema.
tj: i'll prototype token v2 and a validation lib in go/sdk.
mira: i'll PR the routing header attacher, flag-guarded behind `propagate-operator`.
alex: excellent. follow-up sync Wed 11am? will post RFC summary to #architecture and ping eng-sre.
ops-bot: Scheduled: follow-up meeting added to calendar Wed 11:00 (invite: alex,mira,tj,sophie,devon).
